description: Bracket exact-to-tanh GELU interpolation with one FF-output union
proposal: Family: feed-forward width. Current retained frontier is 1,672 parameters at 99.010000%, a +0.010000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 20 prior macro-attempts in this family. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0022 at 3,040 parameters/99.85%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0138, whose alpha=1 tanh-GELU plus output union 82/85 scored 98.99% at 1,671 parameters, while alpha=0 without that new union is the retained exact-GELU frontier. Hypothesis: reducing activation perturbation inside this measured bracket can recover one example while retaining the scalar union. The helper tests alpha 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, then 0 in decreasing order; one candidate per official micro-trial, same 1,671 count, same checkpoint migration. A scored failure makes the next smaller alpha eligible. Stop on the first accepted candidate because equal-count alternatives can no longer improve it, after all four trials, on error, or after eight wall-clock minutes. This is more informative than a new activation because it resolves the near-threshold local boundary.
summary: The monotone GELU interpolation tested alpha=0.5 first with FF-output union 82/85. It qualified at exactly 99.00% with 1,671 parameters and was retained, moving the frontier down by one parameter. Outcomes: 1 accept, 0 scored discards, 0 errors; one official checkpoint migration and verification in about 1m22s. Stop reason: after acceptance, every remaining blend had the same 1,671 count and therefore no eligible strict frontier improvement remained, before the four-trial/eight-minute cap.
